context: The item is a vintage phone, still working perfectly.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I'm interested in the working phone, but don't try inflating the price just because it's labeled 'vintage'. I know what these old units are actually worth, so I'll start us off at 60.

Seller ($185): Sixty? Honestly, I feel sick even hearing that, as this was my late grandfather's prized piece and another collector is already en route to pay full price. I shouldn't even be giving you a second chance, but if you can do 185 right now, I'll tell them to turn around.

Buyer ($80): Trying to guilt-trip me with your grandfather's story and inventing a conveniently en-route collector are the oldest sales tricks in the book. I'm not falling for fake urgency, but if you want a real transaction, I'll move up to 80.

Seller ($168): It deeply hurts that you dismiss a genuine family heirloom as a mere sales trick, but I desperately need to cover medical bills today. I shouldn't even be doing this, but if you can meet me at 168 right now, I will painfully turn down the other buyer's pending call.

Buyer ($105): Switching from your grandfather's legacy to emergency medical bills won't make me fall for another emotional guilt trip. However, since you actually lowered your asking price to 168, I will reasonably step up my offer to 105.

Seller ($155): You're bleeding me dry while my phone literally rings with the other buyer's final confirmation. I am sacrificing a piece of my heart here, but if you can give me 155 within the next two minutes, it's yours before I break down and regret this.
Buyer ($155): Spare me the dramatic performance about two-minute timers and a broken heart. You finally came down to a reasonable number, so I will accept your offer of 155. <AGREEMENT>
